behavior_in_task_description.explanation: This is a deliberately video-grounded task. The instruction says the line must always match the opening settings screen (legend colours, uniform width) and what the fired hook actually does, in every situation. The tests check exactly that: the legend colour, the end point and the width of the line, with expected outcomes taken from the game's own hook physics (start offset, steps, hook_length give-up, tee grab radius). No output files, interfaces or names are needed beyond fixing the existing renderer.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Each of the five defects has its own fail-to-pass test: sub-unit fire speed, wall just past reach, grazed tee, tee behind a thin wall, and diagonal width. Seven pass-to-pass guards cover normal reach, hookable and unhookable walls, a tee straight ahead, a missed tee, a tee in front of a wall, and straight-aim width. Together they cover 'every situation, not only the ones in the clip'.

informative_test_structure.explanation: The test file has a module docstring that explains the method, labelled sections (map writer, screen geometry, Session/Line helpers, and test groups for the line being drawn at all, walls, other tees, and line width), commented layouts that give exact distances, and a descriptive docstring and assertion message for every test.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: Bug patches are applied and deleted in the same RUN step. File timestamps are normalised. Upstream git history is replaced by a single base commit, so the fix commit cannot be reached. Tests and solution are not in the image, and the agent has no network. The tests drive the real client and server and compare screenshots, so string matching on source cannot satisfy them. The protected scripts/ directory is restored before the tests run.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a C++ rendering bug fix; no structured output is expected.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The repo is checked out at a pinned full commit SHA. The rest are apt packages (including python3-pytest and python3-pil installed at test time), for which pinning is not required. No unpinned pip installs.

typos.explanation: Test IDs in config.json and task.toml match the function names in test.patch, and all paths (/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4, /app/build, scripts/) are consistent. test.sh has stale boilerplate comments that mention a 'wx' build, but they have no functional effect.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted right after applying) and assets/recording.mp4. tests/ and solution/ are never copied.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: pytest and PIL are installed in test.sh at verification time. Xvfb, xdotool and ffmpeg in the image are also tools the agent needs to reproduce the bug and inspect the video.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, a real source-code fix (the upstream rewrite of RenderHookCollLine plus reversal of the injected bugs). It does not echo outputs.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent fixes existing source files and does not produce any output file that the tests check.
